title: Affine-open criterion for comparison of unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories

source.place: Tag 09T6, perfect-lemma-argument-proves, statement; equivalence conclusion only, without naming its coherator quasi-inverse.

proof.text: Use the exact inclusion $i_T:\mathcal A_T\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_T)$ and its termwise derived functor $I_T$. The cited Grothendieck result gives exactness of $i_T$; hence $H^r(I_TB)=i_TH^r(B)$, since both cohomologies use the same kernels and cokernels. In particular $I_TB=0$ implies $B=0$. Let $I_T\dashv C_T$ be the derived coherator adjunction, with unit $e_T$ and counit $d_T$, supplied by the coherator node. Both are triangulated and their unit and counit commute with shifts. It suffices to prove $e_X(B)$ invertible for all $B$ and $d_X(E)$ invertible for all quasi-coherent $E$.

source.place: Tag 09T6, perfect-lemma-argument-proves, opening paragraph, the two adjunction maps

proof.text: Say an object is supported on $T\subseteq X$ when all its cohomology stalks outside $T$ vanish. Induct on $n$ with the simultaneous claim: $e_X(B)$ is invertible whenever $I_XB$ is supported on a closed $T$ contained in a union of $n$ affine opens, and $d_X(E)$ is invertible whenever $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ has such support. For $n=0$, these objects have zero cohomology and so are zero; the first step also gives $B=0$. Their adjunction maps are maps between zero objects, hence invertible.

source.place: Tag 09T6, perfect-lemma-argument-proves, hypothesis $H_n$ and base case $n=0$

proof.text: For the induction step let $T\subseteq U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_n$ be closed and put $j:U=U_n\hookrightarrow X$. The flat-interchange node applies to this affine-open inclusion and to the given $\Phi_j$ (the unique unit-compatible identification with its total derived functor is understood). Hypothesis (c) is precisely its normalization hypothesis for $c$. It gives a unit $u:B\to\Phi_j(B|_U)$ which $I_X$, followed by $c$, sends to the ambient open unit $I_XB\to Rj_*((I_XB)|_U)$. Choose cone triangles $B\to\Phi_j(B|_U)\to B^{\prime}\to B[1]$ and $E\to Rj_*(E|_U)\to E^{\prime}\to E[1]$. Existence is the cone axiom; $I_X$ sends the first to a distinguished triangle for the ambient unit, by its exactness.

source.place: Tag 09T6, perfect-lemma-argument-proves, induction step, the two displayed triangles and their canonical first arrows

proof.text: Apply the supported-open-unit cone theorem first to $I_XB$ and then to $E$. Its over-site restriction is identified with restriction to the scheme $U$ by the exact over-equivalence in the restriction-definition node. The open $U$ is quasi-compact, $X$ is qcqs, and $T$ is closed, so all its hypotheses hold. It says that $I_XB^{\prime}$ and $E^{\prime}$ have quasi-coherent cohomology, vanish off $T$, and vanish after restriction to $U$. Thus they are supported on $T\setminus U$, a closed subset of $X$ contained in $U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_{n-1}$. The induction hypothesis gives invertibility of $e_X(B^{\prime})$ and $d_X(E^{\prime})$. This uses no assertion that intersections of affine opens are affine.

source.place: Tag 09T6, perfect-lemma-argument-proves, the cones are supported on $T\setminus U$

proof.text: The affine coherator theorem makes $e_U(B|_U)$ and $d_U(E|_U)$ invertible. In the flat-interchange node put $f=j$ and $D=B|_U$. Its first identity identifies $e_X(\Phi_jD)$, after the isomorphisms $C_X(c_D)$ and $\lambda_{I_UD}$, with $\Phi_j(e_U(D))$; hence it is invertible. Its second identity expresses $d_X(Rj_*G)$, for $G=E|_U$, as $Rj_*(d_U(G))\circ c_{C_UG}\circ I_X(\lambda_G)$, also a composite of isomorphisms. These are the actual adjunction maps, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms between their source and target.

source.place: Tag 09T6, perfect-lemma-argument-proves, last two displays and final affine application

proof.text: Apply the natural unit $e_X$ to the first cone triangle to obtain a morphism from that triangle to its image under the exact functor $C_XI_X$. Its components on the middle vertex and on $B^{\prime}$ are invertible by steps 5 and 4. The two-out-of-three theorem for morphisms of distinguished triangles gives invertibility on $B$. Apply the natural counit $d_X$ from the $I_XC_X$-image of the second triangle to that triangle. Its components on $Rj_*(E|_U)$ and $E^{\prime}$ are invertible by the same steps, so its component on $E$ is invertible. The shift compatibility in the coherator node supplies the last square of both triangle morphisms. This completes the simultaneous induction.

source.place: Tag 09T6, perfect-lemma-argument-proves, application of Derived Categories Tag 014A

proof.text: A quasi-compact scheme has a finite affine open cover. Choose one for $X$ and use the induction with $T=X$ and its number of members. Then $e_X(B)$ is invertible for every $B\in D(\mathcal A_X)$ and $d_X(E)$ is invertible for every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Restricting $C_X$ to that full subcategory gives a functor back to $D(\mathcal A_X)$; the invertible unit and counit are natural isomorphisms between the two composites and the identities, which is the required equivalence.
